thai_P445_nutrition_labelling.content: Notification No. 445 B.E. 2566 (2023), English translation. Clause 2.1: a nutrition claim follows Table 1 (per reference serving size and per consumed serving) for foods with a reference serving, otherwise Table 2 (per 100 g or 100 mL). Annex 2 Category 2 No. 2: carbonated and non-carbonated beverages, reference serving 200 mL. Table 1: free of sodium less than 5 mg; very low sodium less than 35 mg; low sodium less than 140 mg (per serving); sugar free less than 0.5 g (per serving). Table 2: sodium free not more than 5 mg, very low 40 mg (per 100 g) or 20 mg (per 100 mL), low 120 mg or 60 mg; sugar free not more than 0.5 g (per 100 g and per 100 mL). Table 1 vitamins and minerals excluding sodium: good source more than 15 percent of Thai RDI; high at least 30 percent. Clause 2.2: a claim needs an attached statement when sodium exceeds 300 mg per serving. Annex 3 Thai RDI: sodium 2000 mg, potassium 3500 mg, calcium 1000 mg. Clause 8: in force 180 days after gazette publication.
thai_P445_nutrition_labelling.status: sourced (English PDF text extracted with pdftotext 2026-10-18; the Thai text is authoritative; clause-to-table wording on dual basis needs a Thai adviser)

assumptions.text: Sodium, potassium and calcium load is set by CO2 generated, not retained; f_ret = retained/generated
f_ret cases 1.0 (upper bound), 0.5 and 0.25. No source; to be measured
Citric acid molar excess 0 in base case; sensitivity 10 and 20 percent
Stoichiometric reactions: 3 CO2 per citric acid with 3 bicarbonate; 3 CO2 per 2 citric acid with 3 carbonate
1 volume = 1 L CO2 at 0 C and 1 atm per litre of liquid; ideal molar volume 22.414 L/mol (real-gas density basis 22.26 also shown)
Serving 330 ml; drink volume equals serving volume; cube volume ignored
Thai reference serving for carbonated beverages 200 ml (P445 Annex 2)
Henry's law linear to the required pressure; required pressure = V / Bunsen(T)
Open-glass headspace CO2 is 432 ppm (0.000432 atm); equilibrium dissolved CO2 = Bunsen(T) x 0.000432
Base drink sodium is zero for the carbonate-only sodium count; actual base drink not read
Cube contains no sugar and no sodium other than the carbonate; sweetener and flavour are outside this screen
Calcium citrate solubility 0.95 g/L at 25 C applied at serving temperature (4 C value not sourced)
Atomic masses: H 1.008, C 12.011, O 15.999; element masses derived from sourced compound masses

verdict.lowest_sodium_at_usable_fizz: Potassium bicarbonate (KHCO3) with citric acid. The carbonate itself delivers 0 mg sodium. At the 1.5 volume floor and full retention it delivers 864 mg potassium per 330 ml (24.7 percent of Thai RDI). Calcium carbonate also delivers 0 mg sodium, but calcium citrate reaches its 25 C solubility at about 0.13 volumes, so the calcium route cannot reach the 1.5 volume floor without precipitate.
verdict.thai_claim_consequence: Sodium-bicarbonate routes exceed the 140 mg low-sodium limit per 330 ml at every usable target (508 mg at 1.5 volumes, full retention), and exceed 300 mg per 200 ml reference serving at 1.5 volumes, which triggers the sodium disclosure rule. The potassium route has 0 mg carbonate sodium. Its potassium is 24.7 percent of Thai RDI per 330 ml and 15.0 percent per 200 ml at 1.5 volumes (good source needs more than 15 percent; high needs at least 30 percent). At 2.0 volumes it is 32.9 percent per 330 ml (high per 330 ml) and 19.9 percent per 200 ml. Potassium is printed on the Thai nutrition panel.
verdict.reading_caveat: The dual-basis wording of Table 1 (reference serving and consumed serving) is read here as: both must hold. A Thai adviser must confirm it.
bench_test_first: Dissolved CO2 at 4 C and 25 C in open glass, sampled at 0, 30, 60 and 120 s (f_ret per carbonate). This is the measurement that replaces the f_ret assumption.
Gas yield per cube in a closed flask by mass loss, against stoichiometry (confirms 3 CO2 per citric acid for bicarbonate and 3 CO2 per 2 citric acid for carbonate).
Cation content per serving by ICP-OES or flame photometry (Na, K, Ca), with the base drink's own sodium measured separately.
Calcium route only: visible precipitate or turbidity after 24 h at 4 C.
Pass rule to be set before the run by the team; no rule is set in this screen.

open_items: Base drink sodium (Singha Sparkling Water Lime label not read). The sodium-free claim for the potassium route depends on it.
Dual-basis reading of Thai Table 1 (reference serving and consumed serving) needs a Thai adviser.
Whether a dissolvable cube is classed as a food under the nutrition-labelling rules, or under another category, is not settled here.
f_ret (fraction of generated CO2 still dissolved at serving) is assumed, not measured. Every sodium and potassium figure scales as 1/f_ret.
Calcium citrate solubility at 4 C is not sourced. The 25 C value is used. Acid, pH and other solutes in a flavoured drink may change it.
Potassium bicarbonate price: none found. Calcium carbonate price: none found on Makro PRO first page. Lazada and PubChem were not read.
Potassium citrate solubility is not sourced. Potassium citrate concentration is not checked against solubility.
Henry's law is taken linear from 1 atm to the required pressure. The real pressure dependence is not checked.
Thai Notification 447 and 445 text was read in English translation. The Thai text is authoritative and was not read.
Healthier Choice logo beverage sugar limit (5 g per 100 ml) is a logo scheme, not a claim rule. Not applied here.
